bank.question: What two things make up the passé composé?
options: A helper verb (avoir or être) and a past participle
Just the past participle on its own
Two verbs in the imperfect tense

bank.question: Which helper verb does "aller" take in the passé composé?
bank.explanation: Aller is one of the DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs, so it always uses être.

bank.question: Write "I ate" in the passé composé (use "je").
bank.explanation: Manger is a regular -er verb, so the past participle is mangé. It uses avoir.

bank.question: Write "she went" in the passé composé.
bank.explanation: With être verbs the past participle agrees with the subject. Elle is feminine singular, so allé picks up an extra -e.

bank.question: "Nous ___ fini nos devoirs." Which helper verb fits?
bank.explanation: Finir uses avoir, and the subject is nous, so it's avons.

bank.question: Conjugate "aller" in the passé composé with "elles".
bank.explanation: Aller is an être verb, so the helper is sont. Elles is feminine plural, so the past participle agrees: allé + -es.
